Ensemble model spreads from ECMWF and GFS typically encompass this range for a single summer day without a pronounced heat dome or Saharan dust intrusion.

Historical August maxima in Madrid average near 32–33°C, so current guidance sits modestly above climatology yet far below extreme thresholds. With resolution only hours away and no major model shifts reported in the last 24–48 hours, the tight 36–37°C contest reflects genuine forecast uncertainty around the upper end of the expected diurnal range rather than any emerging trend.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus for Panama City, Panama, points to a peak temperature of 32–33°C on August 2 amid the peak of the rainy season, when daily convection and widespread cloud cover typically limit extreme heating. Persistent moisture from the Intertropical Convergence Zone fuels afternoon thunderstorms that reduce incoming solar radiation after midday, while light northerly winds provide modest ventilation. Historical August climatology shows average highs near 29–31°C, so current guidance reflects slightly above-normal conditions driven by reduced rainfall timing in the latest runs. The narrow spread between 32°C and 33°C odds reflects uncertainty in exactly when and how strongly storms develop, as earlier or weaker convection would favor the higher end while earlier cloud buildup caps readings closer to 31°C. Updated NWP output and local observations tomorrow morning will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.
